key_bets: Wiffle-Ball cusp confinement achieves loss reduction factor γ ≤ 0.1 at commercial plasma density (~10²¹ m⁻³), validating the Park 2025 Q≈10.5 projection
Virtual cathode formation is sustainable at reactor-relevant densities without the ~200,000 A electron supply rate calculated by University of Sydney (2019)

Bremsstrahlung losses in a thermalized 20 keV D-T plasma remain below ~5–10% of fusion power, preserving net energy gain despite Park 2025's thermalization assumption (which negates Bussard's non-thermal direct-conversion advantage)
Physics scaling laws derived from sub-microsecond WB-X pulses extrapolate validly across ~10⁶× in fusion power and ~12× in linear scale to a 1.6 m steady-state reactor

MW-class commercial electron beam injectors (78 MW total) can be integrated into a magnetic cusp geometry with high beam-plasma coupling efficiency and acceptable component lifetime under neutron/X-ray fluence
A tritium breeding blanket achieving TBR > 1.1 can be engineered for the polyhedral cusp geometry despite neutron shadowing by the six coil faces
Six-sided non-interlocking superconducting coils at 4.5 T can be built and mechanically supported under asymmetric high-beta plasma pressure loading
eliminated_costs: Divertor system — cusp geometry naturally provides plasma exhaust at cusp points, eliminating the complex tokamak divertor design, replacement, and remote handling costs

Large high-field magnet system — magnets only confine electrons (much lower energy density) rather than 20 keV ions at billion-particle densities, allowing far smaller and cheaper coils than tokamak/stellarator concepts
Fully-remote interlocked-coil maintenance — six independent non-interlocking polyhedral coils enable modular assembly/disassembly rather than tokamak-style fully-remote TF coil maintenance

Burning-plasma auxiliary heating ramp-down infrastructure — the device runs on continuous external e-beam drive rather than ignition, eliminating burn-control and ignition-transient hardware (though at the cost of permanent recirculating power)
novel_costs: 78 MW continuous MW-class electron beam injection system (~$100M override) — not present in any MFE concept; replaces conventional H&CD systems
Tritium breeding blanket engineered for polyhedral cusp geometry with neutron-shadowed sectors aligned to the six coil faces (~$50–200M, vs. ~$7M standard MFE analogue)

Six independent superconducting coil assemblies with custom mechanical support for asymmetric magnetic-pressure loading (~$150M override) — non-interlocking polyhedral geometry has no existing engineering design
Structural recirculating-power penalty (~29% at γ=0.1, 40–45%+ at γ=0.2) from continuous e-beam drive — burning-plasma MFE concepts recirculate only 10–20%
Concept-specific neutronics analysis and likely Li-6 enrichment or thicker blanket sections to compensate for coil-face neutron shadowing

risks.description: Loss reduction factor γ unvalidated — entire Q≈10.5 projection rests on a single free parameter (γ=0.1) that Park 2025 admits has no quantitative model; γ=0.2 drives LCOE to ~20 ¢/kWh or net-negative power

Virtual cathode formation may fail at commercial plasma densities — University of Sydney (2019) found 'little or no trace' and calculated unfeasible 200,000 A electron supply rate; EMC2 disputes but has published no counter-experimental evidence
No energy conversion architecture specified — 80% of fusion energy (~784 MW neutrons) has no defined blanket type, thermal cycle, or coolant; net electric output unknown within ±50%

Tritium breeding blanket TRL 1 — polyhedral coil geometry creates six neutron-shadowed sectors with no proposed solution, no TBR calculation, and no off-the-shelf MFE blanket adaptable; cost may be 2× the $75M baseline
Physics scaling extrapolated ~10⁶× in fusion power and ~12× in linear scale from sub-microsecond WB-X pulses to steady-state reactor; gyroradius scaling exponent flagged as 'preliminary' by Park 2025

Bremsstrahlung-versus-thermalization theoretical tension unresolved — Park 2025's thermalization assumption answers Rider 1995 critique but eliminates Bussard's direct-conversion advantage, an implication unacknowledged in the source

Superconducting coil design for 6-sided cusp geometry has no published specification — conductor type, operating temperature, and mechanical support for asymmetric high-beta plasma loading all unspecified; EMC2 SC work since 2012 unpublished

Company transparency low — EMC2 has published two peer-reviewed papers since 2015, one arXiv preprint, and no current device status; WB-6 fusion result never independently peer-reviewed; no WB-8 results published
No O&M structure, PFC lifetime data, or maintenance plan exists; modular-replacement claim is a design assertion, not a demonstrated strategy

Structural ~29% recirculating-power fraction at baseline γ=0.1 (rising to 40–45%+ at γ=0.2) is permanent due to continuous e-beam drive — compounds γ uncertainty by directly halving Q_eng if γ doubles
Tritium fuel supply — ~55 kg/year requirement vs. ~25 kg global inventory makes on-site breeding mandatory, which in turn depends on the unsolved polyhedral blanket design
